_comment: Canonical claims: rules this repo must state identically everywhere they are relied on. Each entry pins the EXACT phrasings that count as stating the claim; a carrier contains one or it does not. There is no condition/negation inference — #341 deleted it after 24 review rounds and 100 findings with no downward trend. Read check-claims.js's header before editing: it explains why a phrasing must be long enough that no `mustNotMatch` string contains it, which the guard enforces mechanically at load. Adding a legitimately reworded carrier means adding its wording here — that visible edit IS the design, not a workaround.

claims.why: A clean Codex rerun can arrive as a 👍 reaction or as an INLINE REVIEW-THREAD REPLY, and an inline reply never enters the comment list. A file that says only 'check the comments' sends a session to a gate it cannot clear. Round 35 of #294 found that narrowed form in nine files while the source said both — this claim's best case, and the reason it is pinned. The phrasings carry their connector ('so check …', 'predictable: check …') rather than the bare instruction: with the bare form, inverting automations.md to 'so never check …' PASSED, because a phrasing is a substring of its own negation. Measured on #341, not imagined. 2026-09-23 (owner ruling): the non-directive carriers repo-monitors.md, automations.md, ci-triage.md, cicd-setup.md were collapsed to pointers at `directives/git.md` → PR Lifecycle / `docs/standards/pr-mechanics.md` and dropped from `consumers`, so a restated copy is no longer locked in. 2026-10-12 (owner-approved audit R2/R3): CLAUDE.md's restatement became a pointer at git.md and left `consumers`, and every phrasing no tracked file still carried was removed rather than kept as dead wording. 2026-10-16 (owner ruling, #460 step 3): the qa-pipeline command was retired, so it left `consumers`.

Closing it needs a check about STRUCTURE, not wording, so this is the one `raw` claim: it requires the summary sentence to follow the outage bullet with NO further list item between them. claims.why: #336 defined the *unreachable-review test* — the one condition under which a session may take `codex-flagged` off by hand — and then spent three consecutive review rounds being shown a consumer that had dropped it. Round 4: the commit that INTRODUCED the name coined two aliases for it in the same breath. A NAME is undone by a suffix rather than by a clause, so each phrasing pins the character that follows it ('test.', 'test admits', 'test, and') — that boundary is what keeps 'tests', 'tester', 'testing' and 'test-cases' from counting as the name, and the mustNotMatch entries are exactly those four. ⚠️ Pinning the name cannot see the CONTENT of the rule; `unreachable-review-terminal-states` is the entry that does. 2026-09-23 (owner ruling): the non-directive carriers automations.md, ci-triage.md, cicd-setup.md, repo-monitors.md were collapsed to pointers at `directives/git.md` → PR Lifecycle / `docs/standards/pr-mechanics.md` and dropped from `consumers`, so a restated copy is no longer locked in. 2026-10-12 (owner-approved audit R2/R3): CLAUDE.md's restatement became a pointer at git.md and left `consumers`, and every phrasing no tracked file still carried was removed rather than kept as dead wording. 2026-10-16 (owner ruling, #460 step 1): the `codex-flagged` label and its monitor were deleted; the test now names the one condition for merging without a Codex verdict.

claims.why: #299 moved the Codex gate's mechanism out of git.md into docs/standards/pr-mechanics.md, and this is the one must-stay rule the issue named that had no pin: every exit from the verdict gate (the reaction ladder, unavailable, outage) stays reachable, and none clears the gate silently. Both exits lived inside the block being moved, so a split that dropped the rule and left only the pointer would have passed every other claim. Each phrasing runs to its sentence terminator so an appended condition changes the pinned text. ⚠️ Pinning git.md's summary sentence cannot see the list of exits beside it; a refactor that deletes one exit from that list and keeps this sentence stays green. 2026-09-23 (owner ruling): the non-directive carriers automations.md were collapsed to pointers at `directives/git.md` → PR Lifecycle / `docs/standards/pr-mechanics.md` and dropped from `consumers`, so a restated copy is no longer locked in. 2026-10-12 (owner-approved audit R2/R3): the automations.md phrasing, carried by no file since 2026-09-23, was removed with the mustNotMatch entries that existed only to constrain it.

claims.why: The counterpart to the wake gap above: when a run could end without waking the session, the check-in is what keeps the PR from being abandoned mid-flight. Rounds 37 and 39 of #294 were both this claim failing to reach a consumer — round 39's was in wait-gate.sh, which states the rule twice and whose DELIVERED message is the copy that matters. Its carriers word it differently, which is why there is one phrasing per wording and why #341 abandoned trying to infer the shape. Each lowercase one carries its connector: with a bare 'arm the check-in whenever …', inverting CLAUDE.md to 'Never arm the check-in whenever …' PASSED, because ci-notify's lowercase wording matched inside the negation — one carrier's phrasing covering another carrier's inversion. 2026-09-23 (owner ruling): the non-directive carriers repo-monitors.md, ci-triage.md, cicd-setup.md were collapsed to pointers at `directives/git.md` → PR Lifecycle / `docs/standards/pr-mechanics.md` and dropped from `consumers`, so a restated copy is no longer locked in. 2026-10-12 (owner-approved audit R2/R3): CLAUDE.md's restatement became a pointer at git.md and left `consumers`, and every phrasing no tracked file still carried was removed rather than kept as dead wording. 2026-10-16 (owner ruling, #460 step 1): the watcher workflows were deleted and automations.md's restatement went with them, so it left `consumers`.

consumers.why: This file states the rule TWICE — once in its explanatory header comment, once inside the echo the PreToolUse hook actually delivers. The delivered copy carries the most authority: it reaches a session unprompted, at the decision point. Round 39 of #294 was this claim missing here. The header says 'arms a check-in alongside it' and the message says 'ARM A CHECK-IN ALONGSIDE IT', so the phrasing pinned for this claim matches only the delivered form — verified on #341 by deleting the rule from the echo alone, leaving the header intact, and watching the guard go red.
